title: A distributed intelligent decision-making method for game-based adversarial pursuit-evasion of moving target by multiple unmanned aerial vehicles
abstract: To address the challenges of slow decision-making, insufficient adaptability, and limited generalization in tracking moving targets by multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) within complex airspace, this paper proposes an Intrinsic-curiosity and Attention-based Multi-Agent Hierarchical Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (IA-MAHDDPG) algorithm for multi-UAV pursuit-evasion confrontation and intelligent decision-making. First, an autonomous confrontation engine is constructed according to the requirements of the multi-UAV pursuit game, and a decision-coupled trajectory prediction network is designed, which incorporates inter-UAV cooperative information during target trajectory prediction, thereby enabling multiple UAVs to accurately track moving targets based on the current situation. Second, building upon Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG), an intrinsic curiosity reward and a self-attention mechanism are integrated: the curiosity-based novelty is extended from single-agent evaluation to decentralized cooperative evaluation among multiple UAVs, and the intrinsic reward is adaptively weighted in a task-relevant manner, allowing the UAVs to focus on key subtasks while effectively incentivizing target tracking and capture while avoiding excessive exploration. Finally, by incorporating hierarchical reinforcement learning, a semi-Markov decision process is introduced to construct a hierarchical autonomous decision-making architecture, which enables the reuse and transfer of subpolicies and improves the generalization and stability of the pursuit-evasion confrontation. Comparative experiments, generalization tests, and multi-target round-up experiments under various scenarios demonstrate that IA-MAHDDPG achieves good overall performance in convergence speed, encirclement success rate, and generalization capability. The proposed method achieves efficient and stable multi-UAV cooperative tracking and encirclement in dynamic and complex environments, thereby better meeting the requirements of realistic UAV flight missions.

title: Artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse design of low-carbon concrete under carbonation constraints
abstract: This study develops and tests an artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse-design workflow for supplementary-cementitious-material-blended concrete, with artificial intelligence applied to surrogate prediction, uncertainty quantification, dosage-effect interpretation, and multi-objective candidate generation. Optuna-tuned feedforward neural networks were trained on four open datasets and coupled with split conformal prediction, continuous-treatment forest analysis, and non-dominated multi-objective search. The source-aware compressive-strength model achieved a mean absolute error of 7.20 megapascals and a coefficient of determination of 0.687. Under standard cross-validation, embodied carbon achieved a mean absolute error of 2.41 and a coefficient of determination of 0.999, while carbonation depth achieved a mean absolute error of 2.56 millimetres and a coefficient of determination of 0.847. A leakage audit showed that the exceptional embodied-carbon fit is largely attributable to an almost deterministic relation between mixture quantities and the carbon target, although performance was sensitive to source grouping. Continuous-treatment re-analysis showed substantial pre-adjustment imbalance and wide ninety-five-percent effect intervals, so the dosage results are interpreted conditionally rather than as universal causal effects. Three-objective optimization produced seventy-two computational candidates; sixteen, or 22.2 percent, had negative raw carbonation predictions and were excluded from representative reporting. A physically non-negative balanced candidate predicted 75.8 megapascals strength, 141.7 embodied carbon, and 0.064 millimetres carbonation depth. Applicability-domain analysis showed that none of the optimized candidates lay inside a strict joint ninety-five-percent domain for all retained endpoints, emphasizing that the generated mixtures are hypotheses for laboratory validation rather than design-ready prescriptions.
